transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Israeli security forces have detained a large group of activists in the occupied West Bank.
Some are American.
And one of the detained people was New York congressional candidate Brad Lander.
He has now been released.
The activists were there to help Palestinians harvest olives from their groves.
NPR producer Samantha Balaban and NPR correspondent Ruth Sherlock were at the scene.
Among this group of activists, about 80 people, there were American rabbis from the group
Truer, many whom had flown from the U.S. for this, and the Israeli group, Rabbis for Human
Rights.
So they really hoped that they could dissuade attacks from settlers or from the army preventing
them to picking their olives.
The group did manage to pick olives for about two hours, but then we started hearing drones
overhead and the Israeli military and police arrived and declared the area a closed military
zone.
NPR's Ruth Sherlock reporting.
President Trump's special envoy, Steve Whitcoff, is in St. Petersburg.
He's meeting Russian leaders.
He says Russian President Vladimir Putin has released American Stephen Hubbard from detention.
Hubbard is a 74-year-old who was imprisoned in Russia for allegedly fighting for Ukraine
as a mercenary.
Earlier, Whitcoff met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Norway, and NPR's Joanna
Kakissos reports they were joined by Nordic leaders.
The leaders of Norway and Finland both say a fair deal cannot happen without U.S. engagement,
and they're hoping Whitcoff will come back from Russia with something constructive to
lead to that.
Now, the Ukrainians I've been talking to, they do not trust the White House right now.
I hear them saying every day that they believe the U.S. is siding with Russia.
NPR's Joanna Kakissos reporting.
Early voting is underway in Texas.
Democrats hope they can pick up a Texas Senate seat, although it's been more than 30 years
since a Democrat won a statewide race in Texas.
Houston Public Media's Andrew Schneider spoke with Republicans about their choice to support
Republican State Attorney General Ken Paxton over Democrat James Talarico.
Mark Petryczyk from Wood Forest, Texas, says he's supporting Paxton because he's not
Talarico.
I'm a free market guy, and whoever is teaching these kids that socialism and communism is
okay are wrong, and so I'm actually voting against anybody that says they're a socialist
or a communist.
Erika Johnson from the Woodlands says she's backing Paxton because of his record fighting
human trafficking as attorney general.
I do have a friend who was a victim of that, and with his initiative whenever he first
became attorney general, that was really big on my heart.
Most polling shows the race between Paxton and Talarico is a statistical dead heat.
For NPR News, I'm Andrew Schneider in Houston.
You're listening to NPR News.
President Trump will campaign in South Carolina today.
He is supporting Senator Darlene Graham.
She is running for the seat of her late brother, Lindsey Graham.
The state of Florida has executed its 18th death row inmate this year.
77-year-old William Reeves was put to death by lethal injection.
That was for killing a sheriff's deputy in 1986.
From member station WFSU in Tallahassee, Regan McCarthy has more.
A vigil outside the governor's mansion took place at the same time Reeves was put to death.
Peter Cowdery was among the group.
We are here hoping and praying that there'll be an end to all of this.
We don't understand the cadence of killing that we see and this march of death that is
weekly or something close to it, sometimes twice in one day.
It makes no sense.
Florida is on pace to pass its record set last year of 19 executions.
That comes as lethal injection is facing increased scrutiny following a failed execution in Tennessee.
Unlike that state, Florida uses a three-drug protocol.
For NPR News, I'm Regan McCarthy in Tallahassee.
The United Nations is warning the world is not doing enough to stop climate change.
In a new report, the U.N. says the United States is one of the leading emitters of carbon
dioxide and other planet-warming pollution.
The report cites a big demand in electricity and it says more coal is being burned.
President Trump has instructed coal-fired power plants in the U.S. to remain open.
I'm Corva Cullman, NPR News.

Envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg says Putin released American Stephen Hubbard from Russian detention
Witkoff meets Zelensky in Norway with Nordic leaders as Ukrainians express distrust of White House
Texas Senate race: Republicans explain support for Ken Paxton over Democrat James Talarico as early voting begins
Trump to campaign in South Carolina for Senator Lindsey Graham's seat, backing his sister Darlene Graham
